title: Validate what the compiler cannot see
summary: Turn an unknown JSON value into a nonnegative integer or null.

scenario.briefing: A request body claims to contain a count. Validate the unknown value before the import uses it.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.

hints: Use Number.isInteger and a nonnegative check.
Return the original value only after every guard passes.

misconceptions.testDescription: A numeric string is rejected instead of coerced.
misconceptions.feedback: Number coerces strings and other values. It does not prove the input was a number.
Interfaces are erased. Parse unknown input with explicit checks or a schema library.

sections.title: Types are erased before the code runs
sections.body: Interfaces, type aliases, and annotations exist only while TypeScript checks the program. The emitted JavaScript contains no runtime type information. A value from JSON.parse is whatever the text contained, regardless of the interface that describes the intended shape.

sections.title: Guards turn unknown into a type
sections.body: unknown is the safe type for an unchecked value. A guard inspects the actual value with typeof, Number.isInteger, Array.isArray, or a property check. After the guard returns true, TypeScript can narrow the value, and the function can return a precise type such as number or null.

sections.title: Parse at the boundary
sections.body: Validate once where external data enters the program, then pass typed values inward. Reject the value, return null, or raise a domain error rather than coercing it. A schema library can generate the same checks for larger shapes, but the rule is the same: runtime evidence before trust.

vocabulary.definition: Removal of type annotations during compilation.
A check that inspects an actual value before trusting it.
The safe type for a value that has not been validated.
A function return type such as value is Order that narrows its argument.
